title: Stand on the floor of the Colosseum
description: The arena-floor and underground tickets are separate and sell out weeks ahead. Book the full experience or you only see it from the stands.

title: Look up through the open oculus of the Pantheon
description: The largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built, still standing after nineteen centuries. Go when it rains and watch the water fall through the hole.

title: Walk the Appian Way out of the city
description: Original Roman basalt paving, closed to traffic on Sundays. Hire a bike at the park office and ride out past the tombs and aqueducts.

title: See the Sistine Chapel at opening
description: Four kilometres of galleries before you reach the chapel. The first entry slot of the day is the only one that is not shoulder to shoulder.

title: Look through the Aventine keyhole
description: A keyhole in a green door frames St Peter's dome perfectly down an avenue of hedges. There is usually a small queue of people who know.

title: Eat cacio e pepe in Testaccio
description: The old slaughterhouse quarter, and still where Romans eat. Four ingredients, and every trattoria will tell you the others do it wrong.

title: Descend through the layers of San Clemente
description: A twelfth-century basilica on a fourth-century church on a first-century Mithraic temple. You walk down through all three.

title: Climb to the abandoned town of Civita di Bagnoregio
description: A village on a crumbling tufa pillar, reached by a single footbridge. Its nickname is the dying town, and the cliff really is going.

title: Find the hundred fountains at Villa d'Este
description: A Renaissance water garden running entirely on gravity, with an organ that plays using nothing but falling water.

title: Climb Brunelleschi's dome
description: 463 steps up between the inner and outer shells of a dome nobody could explain how to build until he did it.

title: See the David without the queue
description: Book a timed slot; the walk-up line regularly runs two hours. The unfinished Prisoners in the corridor are the better surprise.

title: Cross the Ponte Vecchio before the shops open
description: The only Florence bridge the retreating Germans left standing in 1944. At seven in the morning it is empty and the shutters are still down.

title: Sit in the shell of the Piazza del Campo
description: A sloping brick fan divided into nine segments for the nine merchants who governed Siena. The Palio is run around its edge twice a summer.

title: Drive the cypress roads of the Val d'Orcia
description: The landscape every idea of Tuscany comes from. The road from San Quirico to Pienza at dawn is the one you have seen in photographs.

title: Count the towers of San Gimignano
description: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval tower houses still stand, built by families competing to be tallest.

title: See the leaning tower and then go inside it
description: Climbing it is the part most people skip. The floor tilts under you on the way up, which the photographs cannot convey.

title: Soak in the free hot cascades at Saturnia
description: Sulphur water at 37 degrees pouring over travertine terraces, open all night and free. Go before seven or after dark.

title: Cycle around the island of Elba
description: Napoleon's first exile, and a proper island of granite coves and steep back roads an hour off the Tuscan coast.

title: Get lost in Cannaregio away from San Marco
description: The quarter where Venetians actually live, with the world's first ghetto at its heart and bacari serving cicchetti along the canals.

title: Ride the number 1 vaporetto down the Grand Canal
description: The slow boat that stops everywhere, which is the point. Stand at the back and it costs a fraction of a gondola.

title: Watch glass being blown on Murano
description: The furnaces were moved out to the island in 1291 so they would not burn Venice down. Go to a working studio, not a showroom.

title: See an opera in the Roman arena at Verona
description: A first-century amphitheatre that has staged opera every summer since 1913. The cheap stone steps are the authentic seats.

title: Walk the Alta Via 1
description: One hundred and twenty kilometres north to south through the Dolomites, sleeping in mountain rifugi. Book the huts months ahead.

title: Meet Otzi the iceman
description: A 5,300-year-old man found melting out of a glacier in 1991, kept in a cold cell you view through a small window.

title: Walk the largest high alpine meadow in Europe
description: Fifty square kilometres of rolling pasture at 2,000 metres, with the Sassolungo standing over it. Cars are barred during the day.

title: Drink coffee in a Trieste caffe
description: An Austro-Hungarian port that still orders coffee in its own vocabulary. Ask for a nero and you get an espresso.

title: See the Roman mosaics at Aquileia
description: Seven hundred and fifty square metres of fourth-century mosaic floor under a basilica, walked over on raised glass.

title: Book ahead for the Last Supper
description: Fifteen minutes in a climate-controlled room, twenty-five people at a time. Tickets are released quarterly and go in minutes.

title: Walk the roof of the Duomo di Milano
description: You can walk among the spires and 3,400 statues on the roof. Take the stairs rather than the lift for the better approach.

title: Take the ferry between the Lake Como villages
description: Varenna, Bellagio and Menaggio sit at the fork of the lake, twenty minutes apart by boat and impossible by road in summer.

title: Ride the Bernina Express over the Alps
description: The highest rail crossing in the Alps without a rack, from Tirano up to 2,253 metres and down into Switzerland. World heritage listed.

title: Climb the Mole Antonelliana in a glass lift
description: A lift runs straight up the middle of the dome with no shaft around it, into the tallest museum building in the world.

title: Hunt truffles in the Langhe in autumn
description: White truffle season runs October to December. Go out with a trifolao and his dog at dawn, then eat what you find.

title: Ride the Skyway to Punta Helbronner
description: A rotating cable car to 3,466 metres on the Italian side of Mont Blanc, looking across at the Matterhorn and Gran Paradiso.

title: Walk the coast path to San Fruttuoso
description: A tenth-century abbey in a cove with no road to it. Walk in over the headland from Portofino and take the boat back.

title: Eat focaccia in Genoa before ten in the morning
description: Genoese focaccia is a breakfast food, dipped in cappuccino by people who will not apologise for it.

title: Walk the streets of Pompeii
description: Sixty-six hectares buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD. Go early, take water, and head for the quieter eastern insulae first.

title: See the better-preserved rooms at Herculaneum
description: Buried deeper and hotter than Pompeii, so the timber, doors and upper floors survived. Smaller, and far less crowded.

title: Climb to the crater rim of Vesuvius
description: A twenty-minute walk up cinder from the car park to a still-steaming crater, with the whole bay laid out below.

title: Eat a pizza where it was invented
description: Marinara or margherita, sixty seconds in a wood oven, eaten folded. The queue outside the famous places moves faster than it looks.

title: Walk the Path of the Gods above Positano
description: Eight kilometres along the ridge from Bomerano to Nocelle, six hundred metres above the sea. Walk it downhill westward.

title: Row into the Blue Grotto
description: You lie flat in a rowing boat to get through the entrance. Only worth it in calm seas and midday light.

title: Stand in the Greek temples at Paestum
description: Three Doric temples from the sixth century BC, better preserved than almost anything in Greece, and usually near-empty.

title: Walk the Valley of the Temples at dusk
description: Seven Greek temples along a ridge above the sea. The site opens at night in summer, which is when to go.

title: Walk on the lava fields of Etna
description: Europe's most active volcano, and often erupting mildly enough to approach with a guide. The Sapienza refuge is the usual start.

title: Eat street food at the Ballaro market
description: Panelle, arancine and sfincione shouted at you in Sicilian. Palermo's markets are Arab in layout and still work that way.

title: Sit in the Greek theatre at Syracuse
description: Carved out of the rock in the fifth century BC and still staging Greek tragedy every May and June.

title: Watch Stromboli erupt after dark
description: The volcano has been erupting every twenty minutes or so for two thousand years. Boats sit offshore below the Sciara del Fuoco at night.

title: Walk the baroque staircases of Ragusa Ibla
description: Rebuilt after the 1693 earthquake in one continuous style, stacked down a ridge with 340 steps between the two halves of town.

title: Swim at Cala Goloritze
description: A white pebble cove under a limestone spire, reachable only on foot down a canyon or by boat. Numbers are capped daily.

title: Look inside a nuraghe
description: Bronze Age stone towers found nowhere else on earth. Sardinia has seven thousand of them; this is the one you can go inside.

title: Sleep in a trullo at Alberobello
description: Fifteen hundred conical drystone houses built without mortar so they could be pulled down when the tax inspector came.

title: Swim off the cliffs at Santa Maria di Leuca
description: The heel of Italy, where the Adriatic and Ionian meet and you can see the colour change from the lighthouse.

title: See the baroque stonework of Lecce
description: The local limestone is soft enough to carve like wood and hardens in the air, which is why every facade here is overrun with detail.

title: Fly the Volo dell'Angelo between two villages
description: A steel cable strung between Castelmezzano and Pietrapertosa, crossed lying flat at 120 kilometres an hour.

title: Walk to the basilica at Assisi
description: Giotto's fresco cycle of the life of St Francis, in a double basilica built into the hillside above the Umbrian plain.

title: Stand under the Cascata delle Marmore when they open the gates
description: A Roman-made waterfall of 165 metres, switched on and off to a published timetable because it feeds a power station.

title: Take a boat to the Spiaggia delle Due Sorelle
description: Two limestone stacks off a beach with no road access, under the Conero cliffs. Boats run from Numana in summer.

title: Eat tagliatelle al ragu in Bologna
description: The recipe is lodged with the Bologna chamber of commerce, and it is not spaghetti bolognese. Forty kilometres of porticoes to walk it off.

title: See the Byzantine mosaics at Ravenna
description: Fifth and sixth-century gold mosaic in eight buildings, the best surviving anywhere outside Istanbul.

title: Taste real balsamic in a Modena acetaia
description: Aged twelve to twenty-five years in a loft of shrinking barrels. It costs what it costs for a reason, and it is nothing like the supermarket version.

title: Climb to the lantern on top of St Peter's dome
description: Five hundred and fifty-one steps, the last of them leaning with the curve of the dome, to the highest point of the smallest country on earth.

title: Stand in the middle of Bernini's colonnade
description: Two granite discs mark the focal points. Stand on one and the four rows of columns line up into a single row.

title: Walk down to the necropolis under St Peter's
description: A Roman street of tombs beneath the basilica, with what is held to be Peter's grave at the end. Twelve people at a time, booked months ahead by email.

title: See the Vatican Gardens on a booked walk
description: Twenty-three hectares of formal garden covering half the country, and the only way to see the dome from behind.

title: Be there for the Wednesday general audience
description: Free tickets from the Prefecture, collected the day before. Held in the square in summer and the Paul VI hall in winter.
